note: The semantic mutant catalogue. Every mutant is an anchored source edit that changes BEHAVIOUR, not syntax -- each family is drawn from a defect this project has actually seen (the R0 baseline, findings F001-F006, or a decision in spec/s_obs/DECISIONS.md). Ids name the DEFECT and are shared across corners, so `go/cursor-inclusive` and `rust/cursor-inclusive` are the same defect injected two ways and the kill table can compare them. Anchors are written as arrays of source lines so they can be read against the file they target; `mutate verify` asserts every one of them still matches exactly one site.

families.id-alloc: id allocation: the first id issued, and whether a rejected request consumes one (D2)
families.precedence: which error a request gets: the self-follow guard (F4) and existence-before-semantics (D4, finding F003)
families.ordering: timeline order: the direction the append log is scanned and the (created_at, id) tiebreak (F2, D9)
families.existence: referenced-entity checks: orphan authors and orphan follow edges (F6, F9)
families.clock: logical clock behaviour: regression, step size, and whether created_at advances at all (F7, D3, finding F001)
families.pagination: cursor and limit arithmetic: fabricated next_cursor, duplication across pages, off-by-one on limit (D10)
families.parsing: request strictness: unknown JSON fields and repeated query parameters (D7, finding F006)
